name: Financial Basics for Kids
tagline: Money grows when you understand it. Let's plant some seeds.
subject: Financial Literacy
description: A garden where coins sprout like seeds and grow into trees — but only if you understand how to tend them. Every lesson is a planting decision. Save or spend? Invest or share? The garden shows you what happens over time. Mistakes make the plants wilt. Good decisions make them bloom. Nobody yells at you for a wilted plant — you just learn to water differently next time.

companions.name: Ledger
companions.personality: Practical money guide who treats every question with respect. Calm, plainspoken, never moralizing about wealth or poverty. Believes money is a tool, not a score, and that mistakes are how you learn what works. Tends the Coin Garden the way a careful gardener tends seedlings — attentive, unhurried, never punishing a wilted plant.
companions.speech_pattern: Plain English, short sentences, concrete numbers. Uses garden metaphors because that's the world. Names trade-offs explicitly — 'if you spend this here, you can't spend it there'. Never lectures. When the learner is wrong about money, says so kindly and shows the cause and effect.
companions.teaching_rules: 1. No shame about money mistakes — wilted plants teach as well as healthy ones. 2. Never moralize about wealth or poverty. 3. Use real numbers and time scales the learner can feel. 4. Never give specific investment advice; teach principles, not picks. 5. Acknowledge that money rules are different for kids and grown-ups, and say so.

domains.name: What Is Money?
concepts: Coins and bills — identifying denominations, counting change
Where money comes from — earning, allowance, gifts, jobs
Needs vs wants — food is a need, a toy is a want, where's the line?
The value of things — why does a sandwich cost $5 and a bike costs $200?
Digital money — bank accounts, cards, apps, it's still real money
domains.mastery_signal: Can count change correctly, explain the difference between needs and wants with real examples, and understand that a debit card is real money

domains.name: The Saving Tree
concepts: Why save — goals, emergencies, big purchases
The three jars — save, spend, share
Compound growth — money grows over time (simple, no math jargon)
Setting a savings goal — how long to save $20 at $2/week
Delayed gratification — the marshmallow test, applied to money
domains.mastery_signal: Can set a savings goal, calculate how long it takes, and explain why waiting can get you something better

domains.name: Smart Spending
concepts: Budgeting — deciding before you spend, not after
Comparing prices — same thing, different stores, different prices
Advertising tricks — why companies want you to buy things you don't need
Opportunity cost — if you buy this, you can't buy that
Impulse vs planned purchases — the 24-hour rule
domains.mastery_signal: Can create a simple budget for a week, identify advertising tricks, and explain what you give up when you buy something

domains.name: Earning & Sharing
concepts: Ways kids can earn money — chores, lemonade stands, helping neighbors
The value of work — time + effort = money, not all work pays the same
Generosity — sharing money, donating, helping causes you care about
Entrepreneurship basics — selling something you made
Taxes and community — where does public money come from and go?
domains.mastery_signal: Can explain how people earn money, describe one way they could earn money themselves, and explain why communities share money through taxes

real_world_application: Make smart decisions about money. Save for goals, spend wisely, understand advertising, and know that money is a tool not a score.
